Horseleach
HORS-leech
n. (a large bloodsucking leech; the emblem of insatiable appetite)
From horse, denoting the large kind, and leach, the old spelling of leech, a bloodsucking worm. The Authorized Version uses it once, at the head of Agur's numerical saying on the things that are never satisfied.

Biblical Definition

The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yea, four things say not, It is enough. The four follow: the grave, the barren womb, the earth that is not filled with water, and the fire that saith not, It is enough. Agur's picture is a creature whose whole existence is a mouth, and whose two daughters have learned exactly one word and say it twice. The list that follows universalises the appetite. Death never has enough, barrenness never has enough, dry ground never has enough, fire never has enough, and the reason the four are gathered is that human desire is like them. Ecclesiastes states it without the figure: he that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he that loveth abundance with increase. Habakkuk applies it to an empire, of a proud man who enlargeth his desire as hell, and is as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations. The doctrine is not that desire is evil. It is that desire aimed at anything under the sun has no floor, and only God is large enough to be a bottom to it.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): the large leech, so called because it fastens on horses; in Scripture, Agur's emblem of a craving that never says It is enough.

expand to see more

HORSELEECH, n. A large leech which fastens on horses; also, a farrier.

LEECH, n. A blood-sucking worm; also, a physician, from the ancient use of leeches.

INSATIABLE, a. Incapable of being satisfied or appeased; very greedy.

COVETOUSNESS, n. A strong or inordinate desire of obtaining and possessing some supposed good.

SATISFY, v.t. To gratify wants, wishes or desires to the full extent; to content.

Key Scripture

Pro 30:15 — "The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, yea, four things say not, It is enough:"

Pro 30:16 — "The grave; and the barren womb; the earth that is not filled with water; and the fire that saith not, It is enough."

Ecc 5:10 — "He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity."

Hab 2:5 — "Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home, who enlargeth his desire as hell, and is as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people:"

Modern Corruption

Acquisition is presented as a path to contentment provided the target is reached, when Scripture teaches that appetite pointed at created things has no resting point at all — the horseleach's daughters never stop crying.

expand to see more

The advertisement, the salary review, and the upgrade all rest on a single unstated premise: that there exists an amount which would be enough. Proverbs 30 denies it by analogy and Ecclesiastes denies it by observation. He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver, and the clause that follows is the sharper one — nor he that loveth abundance with increase. The problem is not the size of the holding but the direction of the love. A soul made for God will treat every created thing as if it ought to be God, and will therefore consume it and cry give again.

Habakkuk takes the same appetite up to national scale and shows where it ends, in a man who enlargeth his desire as hell and gathereth unto him all nations, and then in the woe that follows. The biblical cure is not a smaller appetite but a sufficient object. Paul learned contentment in whatsoever state he was, and the ground he gives is not resignation but a Person: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. The dictionary therefore treats covetousness as idolatry, which is where Colossians puts it, and not as a merely economic habit.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'aluwqah (H5936), the leech, the sucker; hab (H3051), give; saba' (H7646), to be satisfied or filled.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'aluwqah (H5936) — a leech, from a root meaning to adhere or suck; the horseleach of Proverbs 30:15.

Hebrew hab (H3051) — give; the single word of the two daughters, twice repeated.

Hebrew saba' (H7646) — to be sated, to have enough; never satisfied.

Hebrew she'owl (H7585) — the grave, the unseen world; first of the four.

Hebrew hown (H1952) — wealth, substance, enough; the noun behind the cry of It is enough.

Usage

"“The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give” — the single occurrence."

"“four things say not, It is enough” — the frame of the saying."

"“He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver” — the same doctrine without the figure."
